clue.text: Gamble on the committee to win all the prizes

parts.note: a sweep is a sweepstake, a gamble where the pooled stakes go to the winners
taken as written
a board is a governing committee, as of directors

explanation.surface: Someone bets on how the committee will vote and hopes to scoop every prize going.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear everything off a gaming table is to take every stake, hence an idiom for winning every award on offer.

clue.text: Charming request not to lose them all

definitions.text: request not to lose them all

explanation.surface: A delightful plea from someone hoping their luck holds at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means appealingly charming; split in two the letters make the gambler's plea 'win some', asking for at least some victories.

clue.text: He clearly conceals his aristocratic origins

definitions.text: He clearly conceals his aristocratic origins

indicators.note: conceals says the next word holds the answer tucked away among its letters

explanation.surface: A nobleman hides his blue blood behind a plain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit inside 'clearly', and the whole clue describes such a peer quietly keeping his rank out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British aristocrat, a peer ranking above a viscount, so he is a man of noble origins.

clue.text: Bound to include everyone. Agreed?

indicators.note: to include tells us one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: bound means tied, as with rope
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A question at the end of a meeting: is everyone committed, are we all in accord?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as a verb of obligation but is the outer piece; the question mark lets 'Agreed' be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tallied matched up, so the accounts corresponded or concurred.

clue.text: No longer plentiful, for instance

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
plentiful means ample

explanation.surface: Something that was once abundant is now scarce, by way of illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate a point, a specimen or illustration.

clue.text: Former student given eid English instrument

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil is presented with a traditional English musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument with a double reed, a staple of the orchestra.

clue.text: What photographic restorers may do if they want another loan

explanation.surface: Photo restorers short of cash hit up their lender for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Restorers touch up damaged prints; and to touch someone is slang for asking them for money, so to touch again is to beg a further loan.

clue.text: Repeatedly show profits

explanation.surface: A firm keeps posting returns, year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means over and over; split as 'a gain and a gain' it describes earning one profit after another.

clue.text: Fail to give notice to castle of power cut

parts.note: a keep is the central tower or stronghold of a castle
during a power cut the lights fail and everyone is left without light

explanation.surface: A castle's lights go out because nobody warned it about the outage.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone uninformed or unaware of what is going on is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Brass hat he may be, but common

explanation.surface: A senior officer who, for all his rank, is quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is slang for a high-ranking army officer such as a general; and the adjective means widespread or common.

clue.text: His missionary zeal rarely allows converts to lapse

definitions.text: His missionary zeal rarely allows converts to lapse

indicators.note: converts is read as a verb, changing the following words into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An evangelist so fervent that the people he wins over seldom backslide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for the faithful but is the anagram signal working on TO and LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary, one sent to spread the Christian faith, like the twelve disciples.

clue.text: One argument against Russian painting

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A single objection raised to a canvas from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional image of a saint painted on wood, typical of Russian Orthodox art.

clue.text: Women's Institute members who show lack of resolution

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the people themselves, the plural noun

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Some members of a women's club prove indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaklings are feeble, timid people lacking determination or nerve.

clue.text: A fit of the sulks is characteristic of the camel

explanation.surface: Sulkiness is typical of a camel's notoriously bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'to have the hump' is to be in a bad mood; and a camel's back bears a fatty bulge.

clue.text: Further occupational therapy must be given to the woman

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A female patient needs more rehabilitative treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Further and additional both describe something else beyond what has been mentioned.

clue.text: Raw recruit in the Ecology Party

explanation.surface: A naive newcomer joins the environmentalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: An inexperienced person is called a novice or untried; and the Ecology Party was the earlier name of the British environmentalist party.

clue.text: Encouraged Miss Davis to feature in a commercial

indicators.note: to feature in means one piece appears inside another

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
Bette Davis was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Someone urged the actress Bette Davis to appear in a television advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Davis' points to the film star Bette Davis; 'to feature in' has her name sitting inside the advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to support or urge on, typically in wrongdoing, so abetted means egged on.

clue.text: Win the right to retain article of terracotta

indicators.note: to retain means one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: to win money is to earn it
the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone gains the right to keep a pottery item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the right' is not one piece: the R comes from 'right' and 'article' supplies the definite article, both kept inside the word for win.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is baked clay, so something of terracotta is made of fired clay.

clue.text: A drop French perfume

parts.note: de is the French word for of, a typical French word
scent means perfume

explanation.surface: A single drop of a French fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or decline downward, a downward slope, is a drop.

clue.text: Grasslands seen as an advantage in South Africa and North America

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but the singular answer names a whole region of such land

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the pair of others

parts.note: van is short for vantage, advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Open plains are seen as a benefit on two continents.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN as advantage comes from tennis, where the score after deuce is 'advantage', shortened to 'van'.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a tropical plain of grass with scattered trees, as found in Africa.

clue.text: Passage provided for trains moving to a junction

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the word before it shift position

parts.note: a T-junction is named after the shape of the letter

explanation.surface: Trains are given a route to reach a railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, a journey or conveyance.

clue.text: Love, he'srich, if eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman will love a man for his money, however odd he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the letters of HE'S RICH; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish is to treasure or hold dear.

clue.text: Redundancy among NUS members makes the hair stand on end!

definitions.text: makes the hair stand on end!
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the short spiky haircut that produces this effect

parts.note: the NUS was the National Union of Seamen, whose members serve as crew on ships
a cut in staff means jobs lost to redundancy

explanation.surface: Job losses among union members cause shock and alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS here is the National Union of Seamen, not students; a cut among the crew is the reading, and the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut in which the hair stands up stiffly.

clue.text: Where the clothes may be dried and agitated

definitions.text: Where the clothes may be dried

explanation.surface: Laundry tumbling in the machine is churned about.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing is spun dry in the drum of a machine; and someone flustered or panicking is said to be in this state.

clue.text: Note I have to deliver

parts.note: G is a musical note
taken as written
've is the contraction of have

explanation.surface: A message saying the writer has something to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over or present something is to deliver it.

clue.text: Charged the Spanish to study

parts.note: la is Spanish for the
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: Spaniards are billed for doing some studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened, as a weapon or vehicle is charged with a load.

clue.text: Minor drawback

explanation.surface: A small disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read as 'draw back': DRAW written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor under the care of a guardian is a ward; and draw turned back spells it.

clue.text: Framework the Head of Geography needs to get free of

indicators.note: head of says we take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: rid means free of

explanation.surface: A school's geography teacher must be relieved of some structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of crossing lines, a framework or lattice.

clue.text: Solid business partnership

explanation.surface: A sound business partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means solid or unyielding; and a company or partnership is called a firm.

clue.text: Neglects regions in a state of disrepair

indicators.note: in a state of disrepair means broken up, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Areas left to crumble are being overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to disregard or pay no attention to it.

clue.text: Cheerful chap making French fries

explanation.surface: A happy fellow working at the deep-fat fryer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means lively and bright; and a person or gadget that cuts potato chips (French fries) is a chipper.

clue.text: Blunt words from the man who can't keep his hair on

definitions.text: from the man who can't keep his hair on

explanation.surface: A plain-speaking remark from a man prone to losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your hair on' is British slang for 'stay calm', so the surface suggests a hothead; the pun is on a hairless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain, unadorned declaration is called this; and a man with no hair makes a 'bald' man's remark.
